Application Materials.content:
When you have completed and submitted the application form, Lancaster will determine the documents needed to assess your application based on your provided information; these will appear in the supporting document section of your application. To be considered, you must upload the required documents marked with a \*. If documents are not in English, you must provide an official English translation and your untranslated copy.
Information usually required:
- **Academic transcript and degree certificate:** upload an official copy of your degree transcript showing the subjects studied, marks, and confirmation of degree award. If studies are not complete, provide an interim transcript. If studying outside the UK and the university’s grading scale is not detailed on the transcript, provide this too.
- **Personal statement:** explain why you are applying for the course, what you hope to gain from your studies, and how it fits with your plans. Recommended maximum: **500 words**.
- **References:** for Postgraduate Taught applications, provide **one reference**, ideally from someone who can comment on suitability for academic study, such as a tutor from previous studies. A professional reference may be accepted if an academic reference cannot be provided.
- **Proof of English language ability:** depending on study location and nationality, applicants may need to provide a recognised English language qualification and upload a copy of the English language certificate so eligibility can be assessed.
- **Passport (International applicants only):** international students who need a student visa to study in the UK must submit a copy of their passport.
When the application form has been submitted, Lancaster will ask applicants to upload documents listed in the **Supporting Documents** section on the postgraduate application portal; required documents should be uploaded as soon as possible, and Lancaster will email if anything further is needed.
For current Lancaster University students or alumni applying to most postgraduate programmes, a reference, transcript copy, or personal statement is usually not required; Lancaster will say if additional documents are needed.

Application Deadlines.content: The majority of our courses start at the end of September/beginning of October. If your course has a different start date, this will be shown in the offer letter and we will let you know when you need to arrive.

Academic Requirements.content:
**2:2 Hons degree** (UK or equivalent). We consider a wide range of degrees, including business, economics, engineering, statistics, mathematics, psychology, geography and sociology, provided that the applicant has had exposure to quantitative methods such as mathematics, statistics, probability, econometrics, game theory, data analysis, operations research, simulation and business modelling, etc. Marks should be consistently at **2:2 level** throughout your undergraduate studies.
For applicants with qualifications from China:
| | 1st | 2:1 | 2:2 |
|------------------|------------|------------|------------|
| Bachelor's degree | 75% to 80% | 70% to 75% | **65% to 70%** |
The grade required will vary depending on the University awarding the degree.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
We require an **IELTS (Academic) Test** with an overall score of **at least 6.5**, and a minimum of **6.0 in each element** of the test. We also consider [other English language qualifications](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/study/entry-requirements/postgraduate-english-requirements/) and if your score is below our requirements, you may be eligible for one of our [pre-sessional English language programmes](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/study/entry-requirements/pre-sessional-english/).
Pre-master's pathways delivered in partnership with Lancaster International Study Centre are designed to improve your subject knowledge and **English language skills to the level required** by a range of Lancaster University master's degrees. Visit [Lancaster University International Study Centre](https://www.lancaster-isc.com/) for more details and a list of eligible degrees you can progress onto.

Program Overview.content:
Business Analytics MSc, entry year 2026, is offered full time over 1 year. Lancaster is ranked 12th for Master's in Business Analytics in the UK and 30th in Europe in the QS Business Master's Rankings (2026), and 8th for Thought Leadership in the UK.
The MSc Business Analytics is designed for students seeking a career in data or business analytics, decision support, industrial engineering or management science. The programme trains students in analytical decision-making, combining the theory of business analytics with practical application through data-driven methodologies and tools. It teaches the entire business analytics life cycle, covering descriptive, predictive and prescriptive analytics.
The programme develops technical, critical thinking and soft skills, including programming in R and Python, statistics, data analytics and visualisation, problem structuring and problem solving, presentation, negotiation and leadership skills. It has partnerships with business analytics practitioners in industry and is continually updated to reflect the changing landscape of business analytics. Students can complete an analytics project that solves a real-life problem as part of the programme.
Lancaster University established the first Operational Research department in the world in 1964, now developed into the Department of Management Science. Academics are leaders in forecasting, optimisation, simulation and stochastic modelling, with expertise in logistics and supply chain analytics, healthcare analytics, sports analytics, network analytics, marketing analytics and pricing analytics.
Key features include practical case-study learning, an industry-based dissertation where students may act as consultants for a company and solve a real-life problem, and the chance to work with companies such as Jaguar Land Rover, Belmond, Costa, Aldi and Unilever. Students take four core modules, one Dissertation module (Research or Industry) and two optional modules.
Lancaster is the only university in the UK that awards IIF (International Institute of Forecasters) certificates after successful completion of the programme. Successful MSc Business Analytics graduates supervised by members of the Centre for Marketing Analytics and Forecasting for their dissertations may be awarded the IIF Certificate in Forecasting Practice, entitling them to use the credential "IIF Certified Forecaster".
A Business Analytics degree can be widely applied across the business world. Recent graduate destinations include Virgin Atlantic, Avanti West Coast, EY, Amazon, NielsenIQ, NHS, Asda, Perch Group, Ascertia, ITV, Sainsbury’s and Serco. Graduate roles include Data Scientist, Business Analyst, Insights Analyst, Account Executive, Financial Analyst, eCommerce Data Analyst, Customer Analyst, Strategy Analyst, Product Analyst, Fraud Specialist, Business Intelligence Developer, Business Consultant and Credit Analyst. Students benefit from the LUMS Careers Team, employer networking events and a strong alumni network.

Curriculum.content:
Duration: **Full time 1 year**.
You will take **four core modules**, **one Dissertation module (Research or Industry)** and **two further optional modules**.
Core modules:
- **Decision Analytics**: focuses on translating real-world business problems into quantitative models and applying quantitative methods and software tools. It introduces optimisation, decision analysis and simulation, with implementation in MS Excel and Python.
- **Forecasting and Time-Series Analytics**: covers forecasting model building in regression and extensions, extrapolative forecasting methods including Exponential Smoothing, and Machine Learning or Artificial Intelligence methods including Neural Networks.
- **Python Programming**: covers sorting and searching algorithms, data manipulation, visualisation, and package extensions such as pandas and numpty, with applications in Business Analytics such as simulation and optimisation.
- **Statistics for Business**: covers probability, sampling, hypothesis testing, regression analysis, model building and model selection, using R and real-world business problems.
Dissertation options:
- **Dissertation: Industry**: an in-depth research project linked to the MSc programme, applying knowledge to a real business problem and delivering a professional research project in a real organisation.
- **Dissertation: Research**: an independent investigation of a scholarly question linked to real business problems, normally involving literature review, research question design, methodology selection and a dissertation defending the findings.
Optional modules include:
- **Machine Learning and Data Mining**: covers the data analysis process, including formulating a project objective, understanding data and resources, statistical modelling and performance assessment, focusing on classification using R.
- **Marketing Analytics**: covers applied quantitative models including customer segmentation, text mining, image analytics and marketing mix modelling.
- **Operations and Supply Chain Excellence**: covers lean principles, Six Sigma, the theory of constraints and statistical process control, plus supplier development and sustainability performance in supply chains.
- **Optimisation and Heuristics**: introduces problem formulations and algorithmic methods for applying optimisation techniques to business problems.
- **Simulation and Reinforcement Learning**: introduces methods for modelling and optimising systems under uncertainty, including simulation and reinforcement learning, with applications such as healthcare services, manufacturing, inventory management and dynamic pricing.

Cost of Attendance.content:
Below is a rough guide to some average monthly living costs (excluding tuition fees) for a single student in pounds sterling. The exact amount you need to live on will depend on your individual needs and prices at the time. The 2025 [Save the Student survey](https://www.savethestudent.org/money/surveys/student-money-survey-2025-results.html) showed an average monthly spend by the survey participants as **£1142 per month** (including accommodation).
- **Groceries:** £146 per month
- **Bills:** £69 per month
- **Going out:** £61 per month
- **Transport:** £67 per month
- **Takeaways and eating out:** £49 per month
- **Clothes and shopping:** £40 per month
- **Holidays and events:** £32 per month
- **Health and Wellbeing:** £24 per month
- **Other:** £26 per month
- **Mobile Phone:** £15 per month
- **Course Materials:** £20 per month
- **Gifts and Charity:** £17 per month
- **Friends and family:** £17 per month
- **Rent:** £529 per month
These figures represent single students, rather than students with families. Other specific costs include laundry: the campus laundrette each standard wash is **£3.00** (+50p for super wash, +£1 for super plus cycle) and each tumble dry is **£1.70**; prices are subject to change in the new academic year. If you will be [living on campus](https://portal.lancaster.ac.uk/ask/campus/living-in-university-accommodation/), check the [accommodation pages](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/accommodation/) to see cost and what is included. International students who require a [student visa](https://www.gov.uk/search?q=student+visa) to study in the UK will also have to comply with the minimum funding required for this.

Financial Aid.content:
There are two separate awards for high-performing students who hold an offer of a place on MSc Business Analytics.
| Study level | Master's-level postgraduate taught students |
| Fee status | Home students, International students ([about fee status](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/fee-status/)) |
| Year of entry | 2026 |
| Based on | Academic or professional excellence. |
| Amount | £5,000 |
| How to apply | Applicants must hold an offer for the Business Analytics MSc programme and complete the application form for their chosen scholarship. |
- The Fulgoni Scholarship is intended for students who can demonstrate either academic or professional excellence. [Fulgoni Scholarship application form](https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?subpage=design&id=Ec2bnHqXnE6poLxzQJAWShmlHnK1jBNBtCov9IMJwEZUMEFVVE9FSFdDT1pYQzRXTkxDSUZISjM0SSQlQCN0PWcu)
- The Robinson Scholarship is intended for an outstanding applicant from a developing country to contribute toward the cost of tuition fees. [Robinson Scholarship application form](https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?subpage=design&id=Ec2bnHqXnE6poLxzQJAWShmlHnK1jBNBtCov9IMJwEZUNEVaODVCNkVGVFpOVzVBMTZGTUpRV1ZINSQlQCN0PWcu)
Eligibility for both awards:
- You must hold an offer of study for the MSc Business Analytics for 2026 entry.
- The Robinson Scholarship is for an applicant from a developing country.
- Applicants must not be in receipt of any other source of funding from an external funding body.
Further information:
- The scholarship is awarded as a tuition fee waiver and is deducted from your fees when you register at the University.
- All offer conditions must be met or exceeded.
- All other entry requirements must be met.
- An offer of a scholarship is conditional upon acceptance by the offer deadline.
- There are no cash alternatives available for these scholarships.
- The award is for September 2026 entry only and cannot be deferred to a subsequent year of study.
- The Fulgoni and Robinson Scholarships can be combined with other Lancaster University scholarships.
How to apply:
- To apply for these scholarships, please fill out the application form for your chosen scholarship before the closing date of **30 June 2026**.
- Successful applicants will be informed of the outcome of their application by the end of **July 2026**.
Related funding page: [LUMS Master's funding](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/lums/postgraduate/scholarships-and-funding/)

Multiple Applications.content: If you have submitted an application and want to change your course, please [contact us](mailto:pgadmissions@lancaster.ac.uk) and we will consider your request. Our online application system allows you to apply for more than one course.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: Requests for a deferral will be considered on a case-by-case basis. If you would like to defer your offer you will need to request this by using our [postgraduate application portal](https://www.e-res.lancaster.ac.uk/postgraduate-applications/Account/Login) or you can [contact us](mailto:pgadmissions@lancaster.ac.uk) by email. If you are requesting a deferral to the following academic year we will not consider your application until we start to make decisions on applications for that year of entry, so it may take a while for a decision to be made on your application.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
Your offer will be either **Conditional** or **Unconditional**:
- **Conditional** means that you have not yet met Lancaster University's academic, English language or any other entry requirements. Details of the offer conditions and how you can meet these requirements will be in the offer letter.
- You can accept your offer before you have met the conditions; you do not need to wait until your offer is unconditional. The offer letter will include a deadline date for making a decision, and if a deposit is required for your course you will need to pay this by the deadline date in the offer letter. If Lancaster has not heard from you by your deadline, they may withdraw your application.
- The deadline for meeting the conditions is in the offer letter. You may have an offer that is conditional on more than one qualification, for example, you may need to complete your university studies and take an English language test. You do not have to meet all the conditions at the same time.
- **Academic conditions:** your transcript and certificate needs to be an official copy and, if it is not in English, you will also need to provide an official translation. Your transcript needs to state your name, the course studied, your marks for each subject, the dates you studied and confirmation that you have completed your studies.
- **English language conditions:** if you need to sit an English Language test to meet the conditions of your offer, you should do this as soon as possible and upload your score to the [postgraduate application portal](https://www.e-res.lancaster.ac.uk/postgraduate-applications/Account/Login). If your English score does not meet the conditions of the offer, Lancaster will automatically consider your eligibility for one of its [pre-sessional English language courses](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/study/entry-requirements/pre-sessional-english/) and will contact you by email if this is an option for you. Lancaster cannot consider you for a pre-sessional course without seeing a valid English language score and does not accept pre-sessional courses delivered by other organisations or institutions.
- Pre-sessional English language programmes are specifically designed to help international students prepare for their studies at Lancaster. Lancaster cannot consider you for a pre-sessional course if you do not have an offer to study at Lancaster University, and needs to see a valid English language score that meets its pre-sessional requirements before considering you for a place.
- For international students who need a student visa, the process for issuing a CAS cannot start until your offer is unconditional and Lancaster has received your passport details.
